en.title: Do two immune-biology scores improve response prediction across urothelial cancer cohorts?
en.summary: Fixed Teff and stromal features evaluated across public urothelial cancer cohorts, with discrimination, calibration, missingness and transport limits.
key_findings: Adding fixed T-effector and stromal RNA scores to a minimal clinical model raised cross-validated response AUC from 0.509 to 0.645 in the development cohort (298 patients, 68 responders).
In the external-source cohort (72 patients, 11 responders), the fixed model reached AUC 0.554 (95% interval 0.367–0.725) and probability calibration was poor.
The two scores support a biological hypothesis worth further study, not a clinically useful biomarker, an individual response probability or a prediction of who benefits from checkpoint inhibition.
en.seo_title: Do two immune scores improve response prediction?

ja.title: 免疫RNAスコアは別の尿路上皮がん集団でも奏効予測を改善するか

ja.seo_title: 免疫RNAスコアと尿路上皮がんの奏効予測
